This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. @Nepal Tourism Board 🙏🏻   #nepalfestival #kukurtihar #tiktok #culture #tihar  Happy GinGin’s Day!🐾 Every time someone says, “If you love your dog this much, imagine how much you’ll love your baby,” I feel like sharing something from my heart. If I ever decide to have a baby, I know I’ll love and care for them just as much as I do for GinGin. But one thing is for sure: GinGin will always be my first baby. His place in my heart will never change. And here’s something I’ve realised: as human beings, when we love someone, we naturally start having expectations. If I ever have a child, as they grow older, they’ll learn to talk, understand things and have their own opinions. I’ll probably have expectations of them too. That’s just human nature. We give so much love, and somewhere along the way, we begin to expect understanding in return. But with GinGin, it’s different. My love for him is truly unconditional. I don’t expect him to understand me, do anything for me or give me anything in return. I just want him to be happy, healthy, loved and by my side for as long as life allows. I don’t need anything from him. Just his little presence, his unconditional love and the privilege of watching him grow old with me. That’s all I ever wish for. Happy Kukur Tihar to my first baby, my little GinGin. May I get to celebrate many, many more Tihars with you. 🫠♥️🐶

🇳🇵 WELCOME TO DASHAIN! Nepal’s biggest and most important Hindu festival, celebrated over 15 days! And ICONICALLY, it celebrates the victory of a powerful goddess over evil. 💅 According to Hindu mythology, Durga, the goddess of strength, courage and protection, battled the evil buffalo demon Mahishasura for nine days before defeating him on the tenth. A whole festival celebrating female power? I’M OBSESSED. 📍 Kathmandu Durbar Square — the historic heart of Kathmandu, home to centuries-old temples and palaces, many of which were badly damaged in the devastating 2015 earthquake and have since been restored. 👑 The Living Goddess (Kumari): Nepal has a tradition of worshipping a real-life young girl as the living embodiment of the goddess Taleju. The current Royal Kumari is just THREE YEARS OLD! She’s selected from a Buddhist family and revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. ❤️ Tika: During Dashain, families come together as elders place a red mixture of rice, yoghurt and vermilion on their loved ones’ foreheads, offering blessings for health, happiness and prosperity. And this is only the beginning of my Nepal adventure… In just a few days, this 34-year-old hag will be attempting to summit Mera Peak at 6,476 metres (21,247 ft) in the Himalayas! 🏔️ No gear, no idea, but plenty of ambition.
